seed: A row of pieces of different widths ran straight off its own edge once there were too many of them, and the only way to get a second line was a grid, which puts everything in equal cells. The walk draws six pieces of six different widths, stacks them into a row, gives the row a width of 300, and turns Wrap onto more lines on.

steps.note: six pieces of six different widths as one row, 10 apart, as wide as they add up to. The Layout section should carry NO Wrap switch, because a row that is the size of its contents can never run out of room, and the sentence under the section should say so.
THE PROBLEM: the row is now 300 wide and its pieces run straight out past its right edge. Wrap onto more lines has appeared, unticked, because there is now a width to wrap against.

THE TEST: nothing sticks out past the right edge any more. The pieces sit on three lines, each line as full as 300 lets it be, the lines 12 apart, and the group has closed around all three rather than staying one line tall. A Line gap field has appeared under the switch.
THE TEST: the space between the lines is its own number, apart from the 10 between the pieces on a line. The three lines move 24 apart and the group grows taller by 24.
THE TEST: widening the row to 560 refills its lines. What fitted on three lines at 300 fits on two here, without anybody moving a piece.
THE TEST: unticking it puts the row back on one line, running out past the edge exactly as it did before, and the Line gap field goes away with it. One undo should take the whole change back.
THE TEST: one undo and it is wrapped again, on the same lines it was on.
